nodes.label: Correctness, budget, regression
nodes.rationale: Three different things that get conflated: does it do what it says, does it fit the time it has, and did it get worse since yesterday. Each needs its own mechanism, and a single performance number answers none of them.

nodes.label: The blind spot a benchmark suite has by construction
nodes.rationale: bench/ measures operations and cannot measure the system they run in. The idle thread cost a full timer period per yield - the whole system roughly a thousand times slower - with every number in bench/ green. Two lessons: latency between operations needs its own measurement, and where a test can run decides what it can see. Measure the floor before believing a slope.

nodes.label: user/bin/latency.lua
nodes.rationale: The measurement bench/ had none of: a yield and a round trip that does nothing. A number that lands on a round multiple of the clock is never about the work.

nodes.label: tools/run_screenshot.py, the display harness
nodes.source_location: The display, from outside the guest
nodes.rationale: Boots QEMU, asks its monitor for the picture being scanned out and inspects it, because some properties are structurally invisible from inside the guest: geometry, the banner, channel order, a pitch bug, real key events, and a detached program still drawing. Sampling intervals aligned to something the system does are how a test comes back green about a screen it never looked at.

nodes.label: The harness: runner on the host, tests in the guest, serial the channel
nodes.rationale: make test and make bench use separate images and runners because -icount makes QEMU several times slower and the tests must not pay for it. Build it at M0 with the first line of output; a harness that is deferred never gets built.

nodes.label: -icount determinism
nodes.rationale: The same spin loop measures 88187, 88687 and 89062 across ordinary runs and 75001, 75000, 75001 under -icount; with interrupts masked the numbers are bit-identical, which is why a 2% tolerance is generous.

nodes.label: The TAP protocol over the UART
nodes.rationale: The guest prints a plan and ok/not ok lines; a forty-line host script launches QEMU, parses the serial and exits with the matching code.

nodes.label: Semihosting for the guest's exit code
nodes.rationale: HLT #0xF000 with SYS_EXIT terminates QEMU with the guest's code, and gives a watchdog a way to abort a hung test. Without it the host kills QEMU on a timeout and guesses.

nodes.label: C self-tests
nodes.rationale: Before Lua exists there is no other option. The special case that must be anticipated when the vector is written: several tests verify that something fails correctly, which needs a handler that records an expected exception and continues.

nodes.label: Lua tests, run at EL0 in a process
nodes.rationale: From M5 the kernel has no interpreter, so the plan and the names stay on the C side and the assertions live out in user/tests/luatest.lua. A failing assertion errors and init prints it; that line is not TAP, so the runner ignores it and a human gets the reason.

nodes.label: Host-driven integration tests
nodes.rationale: Scenarios needing several processes and coordination, where the system's properties get tested rather than its functions.

nodes.label: QEMU and hardware measure different things
nodes.rationale: QEMU is a JIT translator, so wall time in it means nothing - but with -icount it is deterministic, which makes it the right instrument for detecting regressions. Hardware has the truth via PMCCNTR_EL0, and under QEMU the PMU is not faithfully emulated.

nodes.label: What to measure at each layer
nodes.rationale: Each milestone adds its metrics and none are removed: IPC round-trip and context switch, serialisation and GC pause, path resolution and server load, blitter throughput and input latency, query time against file count, and p99 frame time.

nodes.label: Maximum GC pause
nodes.rationale: Not the average: it is the number that decides whether the system stutters, and it will be the project's recurring problem.

nodes.label: Input latency, from the event to the pixel changing
nodes.rationale: The metric that determines whether the system feels good. Hard to measure and worth the effort: a timestamp on the event and another on the flip.

nodes.label: The average lies: record the maximum and the p99
nodes.rationale: A system averaging 8 ms with a 40 ms spike every two seconds feels worse than a steady 14 ms, and it has the better average. A histogram is worth more than a number, because the outliers are the information; the first suspect for a periodic spike is the Lua GC.

nodes.label: bench/baselines.json
nodes.rationale: Reference numbers with date, commit and milestone. A baseline is updated by hand, never automatically, because one that updates itself detects nothing; tolerances differ with the noise - 2% under -icount, 10% on hardware.

nodes.label: Tests as milestone gates
nodes.rationale: Each milestone's definition of done becomes a test that is never deleted, so the full suite is the history of the project and a break in M3's IPC surfaces on the commit rather than three weeks later.

nodes.label: What to resist when measuring
nodes.rationale: Do not measure everything, do not optimise against QEMU, do not chase a number that is inside budget, and do not delete an old test because we know that works by now - that is exactly the test that catches the regression.

nodes.label: tools/run_headless.py, the machine that is not there
nodes.rationale: Every runner attached a framebuffer, so the machine with no display went untested and was silently broken: init asked for a screen grant that could not be given and the refused spawn was the shell. A test suite that always provides every device only tests the machine you have, and the absent device is the configuration real hardware arrives in.

nodes.label: score and sysbench
nodes.rationale: make bench answers 'did this change make it slower' on this desk; score answers 'is this board faster than that board'. Fixed time rather than fixed work, batch size found rather than chosen, units declared rather than inferred from a return value, and a batch size that changes what a unit costs is a broken measurement.

nodes.label: The scores are a geometric mean
nodes.rationale: Because they are ratios: the arithmetic mean of twice as fast at one thing and half as fast at another is 1.25, which claims the machine is better when it is exactly even.

nodes.label: The arrow keys are not broken
nodes.rationale: Written down so it is not chased a third time: every stage of the input path is correct and what fails is the harness, at a different phase each run, correlating with load on the host. A control that shares the variable it controls for is not a control, and a probe must be checked against an input known to arrive.

nodes.label: make powertest
nodes.rationale: SIGKILL five times at five instants during four hundred writes, then boot and ask whether every name reads and every file holds what was written. A missing file is fine; a half-written one, or a name pointing at an inode never written, is not.

nodes.label: tools/test_kfs.lua, the host interpreter
nodes.rationale: kfs.lua is arithmetic over blocks, so with stubs every branch runs on the host in a fraction of a second - including the journal's power-loss window, a few milliseconds that five kills would usually miss. It answers 'is the format correct' and does not replace the guest tests.

nodes.label: A check that survives deleting its rule is not testing that rule
nodes.rationale: Every check was deleted in turn to confirm it fails without its rule. The 'was it committed' test did not fail: the uncommitted case blanked the journal header, so recovery refused it for having no magic and the state field was never exercised. It took three attempts and each wrong one passed.

nodes.label: make browser, a camera with checks on it
nodes.rationale: make web answers over serial because each of its results is a number the guest can say; the browser cannot be, so a page is served from the host, the screen is looked at, and the picture is written whether it passes or fails. The checks are deliberately blunt because a check that goes stale is worse than none, and what the page says is deliberately not compared against a reference.
